problem: The pricing page could render lifecycle controls while showing multiple route panels or malformed mobile route/table content. Two overlapping inline pricing runtimes managed the same state, while a global mobile table selector converted every table on the page into the feature-matrix card layout.
root_cause: Interaction state had two independent inline owners and the legacy mobile table-to-card rule was unscoped (`table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td`). The lifecycle matrix therefore inherited CSS intended only for `.tabelwrap`, and future interaction edits could diverge between the two runtimes.
prevention: Pricing interactive state has exactly one versioned external runtime.
Mobile table transformations must be component-scoped; never target bare table/thead/tbody/tr/th/td selectors in page-level responsive CSS.
Lifecycle controls and panels must remain one-to-one, with explicit hidden, is-active, aria-selected and aria-hidden state.
Responsive regression tests must assert the absence of the global mobile table selector and the presence of component-specific lifecycle card rules.
Production closure requires public /prijzen readback after the merged build, not source-only verification.
